html:
Golkonda was a sultanate in the eastern Deccan of India, ruled by the Qutb Shahi dynasty from 1518 to 1687. Its founder, Sultan Quli, was a Bahmani governor who held the hill fort of Golkonda, first built by the Kakatiya kings. It was the last of the five Deccan sultanates to fall.

Golkonda was famous for diamonds from mines along the Krishna river, and the Koh-i-Noor probably came from them. Its smiths made wootz steel. In 1591 Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah founded the new city of Hyderabad and built the Charminar at its centre. The court wrote in Persian and in Telugu and Dakhni Urdu.

Aurangzeb took the fort in 1687 after a siege of eight months. In the 1700s the region became the core of the Nizam's Dominions.
